newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish TPSA sets closed tender for card phones.
newsitem.headline: Polish TPSA sets closed tender for card phones.

text.p: Poland's telecommunications monopoly TPSA has launched a closed tender for a supplier of public telephones with electronic micro-chip cards, TPSA said on Thursday.
It said in a statement it had shortlisted the British GPT, Greek Hellascom, French Schlumberger and Italian Telefonica in the tender opened January 31.
The firms' offers will be opened at 0930 GMT on February 24.
Rzeczpospolita economic daily reported on Thursday that the value of the contract was about $150 million.

The paper quoted an anonymous TPSA representative as saying the company had not invited four other companies interested in the contract -- Lucent Technologies, Monetel, Premium Trust and Siemens -- because their initial offers were not attractive enough.
According to the daily the winner of the tender will have to produce at least some parts of the telephones in Poland.
